messages.author: 410e477af3aeaf0d
messages.subject: Error using qplot with facets
parts:
Hi,

I've been having some problems trying to plot some data I've got using
the facets argument in qplot. It always returns the same error:
Error in if (empty(df)) return(data.frame()) :
missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

I'm not sure what I should be doing to my data to make it compatible.
It doesn't contain any NA values. I pruned down my original data set
(using head) to just a small selection containing only two relevant
columns and it still produces the same error.

My data is:
result time.ms
Inconclusive 397
Inconclusive 225
Found 9
Found 8
Found 13
Found 17

I'm trying to do the following:
my.data <- read.table("data.txt", header = TRUE)
library(ggplot2)
qplot(time.ms, data = my.data, facets = result ~ ., geom =
"histogram")

Can anyone advise me on what I should be doing to make qplot happy
with my data.
Thanks,
Alastair

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: Error using qplot with facets
parts:
Hi,

Easy way to avoid this error is to using variable name other than
"result" as follows:
names(my.data)[1]<-"RESULT"


to the author of reshape package:

I don't know whether this bug has been already reported,
a bug in reshape1 seems to induce this error:

r <- if (!df)
unlist(result$result)
else result$result

should be

r <- if (!df)
unlist(result$results)
else result$results

but maybe variable name "results", which is generated in condense.df,
is confusing because many user may want to use this name for labeling
their data.
I think more unique and meaningless name is preferable for internal
use to avoid the conflict.
Actually it induces an error when i call reshape1 using the variable
name "results".

HTH.

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: Error using qplot with facets
parts:
Sorry, not the name "results" but "result" induce an error.
Here is a reproducible example.

> dat<-data.frame(a=gl(2,2),result=gl(2,2),value=rnorm(4))
> reshape1(dat,list("a",NULL),mean)
a (all)
1 1 -0.2702277
2 2 -0.7290297
> reshape1(dat,list("result",NULL),mean)
Error in order(result = list(-0.270227651838571, -0.729029716491266)) :
unimplemented type 'list' in 'orderVector1'

and please try this:
> reshape1(dat,list("a",NULL),mean,df=TRUE)
(all)
1 Numeric,3
2 Numeric,3
> reshape1(dat,list("result",NULL),mean,df=TRUE)
(all)
1 "1"
2 "2"

the last example does not induce the error, but the result seems to be
incorrect.

Now i'm not sure if the patch in the previous mail is correct.
Actually I'm confusing, but it seems to be a bug.

The return value of condense() includes "$result", while those of
condense.df() includes "$results".
In reshape1, there is dispatch depending on the argument "df"

if (!df) {
data.r <- expand(condense(data, variables, fun.aggregate,
...))
}
else {
data.r <- condense.df(data, variables, fun.aggregate,
...)
}

so data.r has either "$result" or "$results"
then, after some conversion,

I think these codes induce the error and undesired result, but i have
no idea how the code should be fixed.
As i said, using unique and meaningless name instead of $result and
$results may be one pragmatic (but not beautiful) solution
